title: Adapter Integration Governance and Starter Kit
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This page defines the governance rules, starter kit contents, and operational patterns for building and shipping "adapters" — small integration components that adapt customer code, third-party data sources, or edge runtimes to Redwood SDKs and the Redwood serving runtime. It consolidates SDK guidance, quickstart steps, canonical API examples, docs-site requirements, and the top support fixes we apply when adapters fail in production.

Purpose and audience:
- Purpose: Reduce integration friction, eliminate repeated support patterns, and ensure adapters meet observability and reliability expectations before being surfaced in public SDK examples or the Docs site.
- Audience: SDK integrators, partner engineers, developer advocates, support engineers, and platform reviewers.

Key goals:
- Provide a minimal, production-ready adapter starter kit with clear patterns for retries, backpressure, and credential handling.
- Define observability and SLO requirements for adapter owners.
- Publish canonical API examples that demonstrate safe failure modes and graceful degradation.
- Give quick operational playbooks for common support issues and a checklist for docs-site publication.

Scope:
- Applies to: HTTP adapters, streaming adapters (websocket/gRPC), on-prem data connectors, and small language-specific shim libraries that wrap the Redwood API.
- Not in scope: core runtime changes, infra-level networking or firewall config (see eng-infra runbooks).

Starter kit contents (repo layout):
- README.md — Quick overview and compliance checklist.
- /examples — 3 small examples: webhook-adapter, streaming-proxy, onprem-file-ingest.
- /templates — adapter.toml (manifest), Dockerfile, GitHub Actions workflow, licensetemplate.
- /observability — sample OTLP config, prom-exporter example, example metrics.yaml.
- /tests — local contract tests and CI smoke tests (tokenized).
- /docs — docs-site-ready markdown, snippet validation test.

Minimum acceptance checklist before merge to main (required):
1) Security review: credentials must be provisioned via env vars or Redwood secret provider; no inline secrets.
2) Observability: adapter exports the three required metrics (requests_total, request_latency_ms, request_errors_total) with labels: adapter_name, region, environment.
3) SLOs declared in adapter.toml: 99.5%% p95 latency for non-streaming calls; 99%% availability per week.
4) Retry/backoff: exponential backoff with jitter implemented; idempotency checks for retryable operations.
5) Contract tests: runs locally in CI against a stubbed runtime; golden traces recorded.
6) Docs: example usage with code sample, quickstart with 3 CLI commands, and a short troubleshooting section.

Quickstart (3-minute onboarding):
1) Clone the starter kit:
   git clone git@github.com:redwood-integration/starter-adapter.git my-adapter
2) Bootstrap and run local stubbed runtime (uses docker-compose):
   cd my-adapter && ./scripts/bootstrap-local.sh
3) Run contract tests and the sample example:
   ./scripts/run-contract-tests.sh && ./examples/webhook-adapter/run-local.sh

API example (safe generation + fallback) — JSON snippet for Docs site:
{
  "request": {
    "prompt": "Summarize the payload and return status code",
    "timeout_ms": 2500
  },
  "fallback": {
    "type": "static_summary",
    "message": "The integration could not reach the external source; returning cached summary."
  }
}

SDK integration patterns (recommended):
- Initialization: make network clients lazily and share per-process to avoid excess FDs.
- Token refresh: use background refresh with a 30s pre-expiry window.
- Batching: accumulate small messages for the runtime batching header; expose batch_size hints in config.
- Streaming: always support resume tokens where possible; reconciliate resume token expiry cases with a 410 handler.

Observability and telemetry requirements (table):
- metrics: requests_total, request_latency_ms (histogram), request_errors_total
- traces: instrument entry, external call, and adapter handler spans; include trace_id in logs
- logs: structured JSON with keys: ts, level, adapter, correlation_id, msg
- tracing sample rate: default 10%%; configurable per-environment

Operational SLOs and thresholds:
- Availability: 99%% weekly (alert when <99.5%% in 24h window).
- Latency: p95 < 500ms for small webhooks; p95 < 2000ms for long-running file ingest.
- Error budget: 1%% of requests per week; auto-rollbacks triggered if error budget burn rate > 3x for 1h.

Docs site publication checklist (for docs engineers):
1) Validate snippets with snippet-runner (see /scripts/snippet-validate.sh).
2) Mark code samples with language and input tokens.
3) Add cross-links to API examples and the adapter manifest spec.
4) Run docs-site preview and smoke test on staging.

Canonical fixes and top support issues (triage playbook):
- Issue: Adapter times out intermittently under burst load.
  Fixes applied: enable concurrency limit in adapter config, switch to connection pooling, add histogram metrics, and recommend an autoscaling policy for dedicated pools.
- Issue: Duplicate messages after retry.
  Fixes applied: add idempotency keys in requests; if idempotency unknown, downgrade to at-most-once and document limitations.
- Issue: Missing traces in backend.
  Fixes applied: ensure trace context is propagated on all async handoffs; add small trace debug helper to capture sample payloads.

Failure isolation and rollback steps (runbook):
1) Detect: Alert via PagerDuty if request_errors_total spike > 200%% baseline for 5m.
2) Mitigate: Disable adapter variant in routing (console: Deployments -> Adapter pool -> disable) and route to fallback adapter.
3) Rollback: Re-deploy previous artifact via GitHub Actions rollback workflow: .github/workflows/rollback.yml -> run with tag previous-stable.
4) Postmortem: Owner documents RCA in /confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues and attaches logs/traces and decision record.

Support handoff template (for L2):
- Summary: one-line description of the failure.
- Impact: customers affected, perceived SLA impact.
- Evidence: links to traces, metric charts, recent deploys.
- Mitigation steps taken: list.
- Next steps: owner, timeline for fix, rollback strategy.

Ownership and contacts:
- Primary owner: eng-integration-team (oncall: @eng-integration-oncall)
- SDK liaison: Marco Chen (marco@redwood.com)
- Docs reviewer: Elena Ruiz (elena@redwood.com)

Appendix — adapter.toml minimal example (manifest):
[adapter]
name = "webhook-transformer"
version = "0.1.0"
maintainer = "team-integration@redwood.com"
slos = ["latency_p95:500ms", "availability:99%"]
metrics = ["requests_total", "request_latency_ms", "request_errors_total"]

Troubleshooting quick commands:
- Collect compressed logs for last 2h:
  ./scripts/collect-logs.sh --since 2h --output /tmp/adapter-logs.tar.gz
- Run local load replay (100 req/s for 2m):
  ./scripts/load-replay.sh --rate 100 --duration 120
- Validate metrics exported to OTLP endpoint:
  curl -fS $OTLP_ENDPOINT/metrics/health || echo "OTLP unreachable"

Change governance for adapters:
- Any adapter intended for public docs/examples must pass the starter-kit checklist and be listed in the integrations index.
- Major changes (behavioral or API surface) require a short ADR and one-week staged canary rollout.

Related resources:
- Starter kit repo: git@github.com:redwood-integration/starter-adapter.git
- Observability spec: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/adapter-observability-spec
- Support triage playbook: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues/adapter-triage-playbook

If you are integrating a new adapter and need a review, open a PR against the starter kit and tag @eng-integration-team; use the label adapter-review and include the acceptance checklist in the PR description.
